subject: english-literature
title: Post-Structuralism and the Reader
welcome_lead: Meaning slips, the author dies, the reader writes the text. Welcome to post-structuralism and reader-response.
meta_desc: Post-structuralism, reader-response and Barthes at A-Level English Literature.
final_note: You have read with Barthes, Derrida and Iser — and seen meaning as collaborative, deferred, plural.

concepts.def: Movement (Derrida, Barthes, Foucault) destabilising structuralist certainties about meaning, sign and subject.
Roland Barthes (1967) — the author does not control meaning; the reader produces it.
Jacques Derrida's strategy for reading the contradictions and supplements within seemingly stable binaries.
Approach (Iser, Fish) treating meaning as produced in the reader's encounter with the text.
Wolfgang Iser's idea that texts contain gaps the reader fills, constituting an implied reader role.
Stanley Fish's term — meaning is determined by communities of readers sharing interpretive strategies.

walkthroughs.body_html: Barthes's 1967 essay The Death of the Author argues that to assign a text its author closes its meaning. Texts are tissues of citation; the reader is the site where their plurality coheres.

Derrida's différance (1968) names meaning's deferral and difference. No sign rests on a stable referent; meaning unfolds through endless substitution.

Deconstructive reading shows how texts undermine their own apparent oppositions.
Iser argued texts present a structure of gaps that readers fill. Fish radicalised this — interpretive communities, not texts, generate meaning.
